title: Singular genitive with consonant gradation
summary: Use the weak stem before singular -n in these words: katu (“street”) → kadun.
objectives: Use the weak stem before singular -n in these words: katu (“street”) → kadun.

sections.title: Meaning and pattern
paragraphs: The genitive is a case form. It can link a word to an owner or another noun. Here you practise the word form; later lessons show its uses in sentences.
Use the weak stem before singular -n in these words. The changes are t → d, pp → p, kk → k, p → v, lt → ll, nt → nn and nk → ng; learn which change belongs to each word.
keyPoints: Learn the word with its stem; the last letter alone does not identify every pattern.

steps: Change t to d: katu → kadu-; add -n to get kadun.
The form changes the grammatical use, while the word keeps its basic meaning.
Change pp to p: kauppa → kaupa-; add -n to get kaupan.
The form changes the grammatical use, while the word keeps its basic meaning.
Change kk to k: pankki → panki-; add -n to get pankin.
The form changes the grammatical use, while the word keeps its basic meaning.
Change t to d and keep i: äiti → äidi-; add -n to get äidin.
The form changes the grammatical use, while the word keeps its basic meaning.
Change p to v and keep ä: leipä → leivä-; add -n to get leivän.
The form changes the grammatical use, while the word keeps its basic meaning.
Change lt to ll: silta → silla-; add -n to get sillan.
The form changes the grammatical use, while the word keeps its basic meaning.
Change nt to nn: ranta → ranna-; add -n to get rannan.
The form changes the grammatical use, while the word keeps its basic meaning.
Change nk to ng: kenkä → kengä-; add -n to get kengän.
The form changes the grammatical use, while the word keeps its basic meaning.

commonMistakes: Learn the word with its stem; the last letter alone does not identify every pattern.
Keep the requested number: singular is one, plural is more than one.
A slash between model forms marks accepted alternatives; write just one form.

practiceExercises.prompt: Complete the singular genitive of katu (“street”): kadu____. Write only the missing letter.
practiceExercises.explanation: Change t to d: katu → kadu-; add -n to get kadun.

practiceExercises.prompt: Complete the singular genitive of kauppa (“shop”): ____n. Write only the letters before the final n.
practiceExercises.explanation: Change pp to p: kauppa → kaupa-; add -n to get kaupan.

practiceExercises.prompt: Practise the singular genitives in order, separated by a comma: kenkä (“shoe”); ranta (“shore”).
practiceExercises.explanation: Change nk to ng: kenkä → kengä-; add -n to get kengän. Change nt to nn: ranta → ranna-; add -n to get rannan.
